Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:65: To examine the matter more precisely, the phrase "He is God" may be understood through what my master, may his rest be in Eden, explained on what the Rashbi wrote (Zohar, Beshalach 46a) regarding "the darkness of morning" — he explained that the intent is that the attribute of night is included within day and the attribute of day within night. That is, in the day, when it wishes to shine, there is first darkness, to show that although the attribute of day has come, the attribute of night is nonetheless included with it. And when the sun comes, when it would be fitting for night to fall immediately, instead the sun shines, to show that it is included in the attribute of night. This is the meaning of "YHVH is God" — that YHVH is itself included within "God," and "God" is YHVH; all is a single unity.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:66: And what the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Va'era 26b) in interpreting the verse "and you shall take it to your heart [levav]" — that "levav" [with its doubled letter] alludes to right and left, the good inclination and the evil inclination — this too connects with "and you shall know this day," whose meaning is that right and left are bound up with day and night, right with day and left with night, as the Rashbi explained (ibid., Shemot 18b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:67: In this a little of the much that pertains to the contemplation of the world has been included. Let us now proceed to explain the matter of contemplation regarding man, in a chapter of its own:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:1: Concerning the contemplation of man's creation and his conduct until his day of death, and his good reward after death — we learned in Tractate Avot (3:14): He used to say, beloved is man, for he was created in the [divine] image; but it is a sign of extra love that it was made known to him that he was created in the image, as it is said (Genesis 9:6), "for in the image of God He made man." Now, the apparent redundancy of the Mishnah's language requires explanation: what does it add by saying "it is a sign of extra love that it was made known to him that he was created in the image" beyond what it already said at first, "beloved is man, for he was created [in the image]"?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:2: What occurs to me on this is based on what the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Tikkunei Zohar 130b), which we quoted in the Gate of Fear, chapter 9 — that man is called a "small world," and all his limbs are arranged according to the order of the works of creation. In the Gate of Holiness we explained the particulars of each limb individually; see there. And in general, the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar Chadash on Song of Songs (74a), in these words: "'Let us make man in our image, according to our likeness' (Genesis 1:26) — it is written (Psalms 37:23), 'A man's steps are established by the Lord, and He delights in his way.' Come and see: when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the upper world and the lower world, all was in a single pattern, so that this would correspond to that. When the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to create man below, He wished to make him correspond to the two worlds, and all the secrets above and below are all in man. The skull of the head resting upon the body is in the mystery of the upper world, in those configurations of the head. The body is in the mystery of the body, where the grades reside in known limbs beneath this head. The thighs and legs are all in the lower grades, as befits him to be in the pattern of what is above and to be in the pattern of what is below. And all the patterns, upper and lower, the Holy One, blessed be He, engraved them all in man, so that he be complete in everything." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:3: And in the Tikkunim (p. 123a) he explained another way, in these words: "These limbs are all in the sefirot: the head is Keter Elyon; the brain is Chochmah; Binah is the heart, and in it is an understanding heart; the two arms are Chesed and Gevurah; the body is the central column; the two legs are Netzach and Hod; Yesod is the membrum, the Shechinah is its sign [i.e., the sign of the covenant]." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:4: In particular, one who studies the wisdom of truth [Kabbalah] will discern the workings of man's creation more than other scholars — when he studies the Idra and learns the reason why a man has a beard and a woman does not, and other such differences; and the matter of the thirty-two years [of the moon's cycle reflected in the body] and the tongue set in the middle [of the mouth]; and the three colors of the eye; and the shaping of the ear, made with chambers; and ten fingers on the hands, neither eight nor six; and likewise twenty-eight joints; and likewise the windpipe and gullet — the windpipe having six rings, and the gullet white within and red without, which alludes to YHVH-Adonai; and man's walking upright on his feet, not going on the ground like an animal, because of his rank being like that of the angels, who stand, as it is said (Isaiah 6:2), "Seraphim stood above Him," and it is said (Zechariah 3:7), "I will give you places to walk among these that stand."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:5: The matter of the [facial] lines that the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (Yitro, in the section "And you shall see" 76b) and in the Tikkunim (121a) surely indicates the Holy One, blessed be He's, providence over man, whom He created with supernal wisdom — as we bless, "Who forms man in wisdom"; see there. And regarding this contemplation it says, "beloved is man, for he was created in the image," namely, in [the pattern of] Atzilut, and all of it is in his body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:6: Even according to the plain sense, providence is evident here, as it is said (Psalms 94:9), "He who plants the ear, shall He not hear? He who forms the eye, shall He not see?" And the interpretation of "who plants the ear" is precise, using the term "planting" for the ear and "forming" for the eye — because the ear resembles a planted tree, which has roots below and a branch growing out above; so too the ear is made with supernal wisdom, for if the ear were created only for hearing sound, it would suffice to have a single opening without the formation extending outward — the lower lobe and the surrounding cartilage shaped as we see. Rather, surely it is like a planted tree, in that as the root goes, so the branch emerges; so too, according to what is rooted in potential in the brain, of necessity that pattern must emerge outward and form the shape of the ear. The same applies to the other particular senses of man, for the senses are like the soul residing in the brain, manifesting outward in this pattern — for as the root goes, so the branch emerges. And it says "who forms the eye," because we observe that the eye has a pattern of three colors, which according to the plain sense is unnecessary; yet since the Holy One, blessed be He, formed it in this pattern, "shall He not see" — this shows His constant providence over man and over his particulars. And when you examine this by the way of the secret, you will find that the place where the ear is planted and the eye is shaped is in the attributes and functions of sight and hearing, which depend on the soul clothed within them — understand this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:7: "It is a sign of extra love that it was made known to him that he was created in the image" refers to the inward reality of the soul; and so it is explained in the Tikkunim (94b) that the soul is called "image" [tzelem], in these words: "Rabbi Elazar said: but regarding the Shechinah, is it not written of her creation [beri'ah], but rather Atzilut, and it should have said 'And Adonai created man' — why 'Elohim'? Rather, the Shechinah is called Elohim, and regarding that soul given to a person it says, 'And Elohim created man in His image,' in the pattern of the Shechinah. And regarding that soul it is said (Psalms 39:7), 'Surely man walks about in tzelem [an image]' — for at the time the soul departs from a person, it cannot move on its own. He said to it: Blessed is my son to the Ancient of Days. And My son, whoever damages this pattern, it is as though he diminishes the Image, and the Shechinah does not dwell there. And the secret of the matter is (Deuteronomy 31:17), 'Is it not because my God is not within me that these evils have found me' — the evils found me because the Shechinah has departed from me." — end of quotation. Here it is stated explicitly that the soul is called "image."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:8: With this, the Mishnah's language may be examined precisely — for when it comes to speak of the matter of the soul, which is a part of Him, blessed be He, it says "it is a sign of extra love that it was made known to him" — to him alone, and not to the other creatures, not even the angels; for regarding man it says (Genesis 2:7), "and He blew into his nostrils the breath of life," and we quoted the statement of the Idra on this verse in chapter 11 [of the Gate of Fear]; and there is further support for this interpretation in the Tikkunim. And there (p. 116b) they explained a second interpretation regarding (Genesis 1:27), "And Elohim created man in His image, in the image of Elohim" — saying: "in His image" is the lower Shechinah; "in the image of Elohim" is the upper Shechinah. In this manner one may also explain the Mishnah's doubled phrasing, and it is understandable.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:9: Another possible interpretation is based on what the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Emor 104b) regarding (Psalms 39:7), "Surely man walks about in an image" — see there — that this refers to another dimension besides the soul itself, something like a garment for the soul, and from this "image" comes the splendor of a person's face. This, then, is "beloved is man, for he was created in the image" — namely, this image; and "it is a sign of extra love etc." refers to the soul itself, as I explained. This is the general scheme regarding the aspect of the body and the aspect of the soul. Also, regarding the components of his soul, one finds in him nefesh, ru'ach, neshamah, of the category chayah and kise [chair/throne], as explained in the Tikkunim; and if he merits more, he is given ru'ach, nefesh, and neshamah from Atzilut. Thus man encompasses all existing things, whether in the externality of his body or in the interiority of his soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:10: Therefore, when a person perfects his deeds and does not damage them, it is inevitable that the Holy One, blessed be He, will be found with him, as it says in the psalm "He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High" (Psalms 91:15), "for He will deliver you... he shall call upon Me, and I shall answer him; I am with him in distress." Now, from these two aspects, the Holy One, blessed be He, is called Father to man, and man is a son; and perhaps this is what the verse intends in saying (Deuteronomy 32:6), "Is He not your Father who acquired you" — from the aspect of the soul; "He made you and established you" — from the aspect of the body. There is some proof for this from the words of our sages, of blessed memory (Yalkut, Iyov, remez 914), as we quoted in the Gate of Fear, chapter 3.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:11: Now from this aspect a great love for the Holy One, blessed be He, is awakened, in that He fashioned man in His image so that He might be found with him even though he is below, in the world of Asiyah. We shall not speak here of the wonders of God in forming the fetus in its mother's womb, on which our sages, of blessed memory, elaborated greatly — for this matter is mostly homiletical, and whoever wishes to seek it out will find it in the Yalkut (Yalkut Shmuel, siman 83), on Hannah's verses, "There is no Rock like our God"; and further in Vayikra Rabbah, parashat "When a woman conceives" (14:9); and further in Iyov (10:12), on the verse "You have granted me life and lovingkindness."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:12: Further: why is the fluid of the eyes salty, and the fluid of the ears oily; why is the fluid of the nose foul-smelling, and the fluid of the mouth sweet — all this is explained in the Yalkut (on Psalm 33, siman 720), on the psalm "Sing joyfully, O righteous" (Psalms 33), on the verse "He gathers the waters of the sea as a heap, placing the depths in storehouses."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:13: There is yet another aspect that a person should contemplate regarding the formation of man, namely what our sages, of blessed memory, said: "there is no Rock like our God" — do not read "tzur" [Rock] but "tzayar" [Artist] — for He created many faces among human beings, and no face resembles its fellow. The reason for this is that just as souls differ at their source — for they are six hundred thousand holy souls, generally grouped as the face of a lion, the face of an ox, the face of an eagle, the face of a man; and within the lion-type there are several sub-aspects, and likewise within the ox-type — so the faces below likewise differ. And this is a branch of the wisdom of physiognomy, to know who derives from the lion-type, etc. In the Tikkunim (66b) it says: "Whoever bears the imprint of a lion in his seal has a white face; whoever bears the seal of an ox has a ruddy face; whoever bears the seal of an eagle has a greenish face; whoever bears the seal in the pattern of man is dark-faced, in the manner of the Torah, of which it is said (Song of Songs 1:5), 'I am dark, but comely.'" — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:14: Of this same category is what our sages, of blessed memory, said in Bereishit Rabbah (36:7) about Canaan, that he emerged blackened, as it says of him (Genesis 9:25), "Cursed be Canaan" — because Ham castrated his father, and Canaan told his two brothers outside. And they said there, Rabbi Huna in the name of Rabbi Yosef: You prevented him from doing something that is [done] in darkness; therefore that man shall be ugly and blackened. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:15: Let us return to the exposition we were engaged in, and say: certainly, on account of all the aspects mentioned above, it is fitting that the Holy One, blessed be He, be called our Father, our King, and that we be called sons to Him, as it is said (Deuteronomy 14:1), "You are sons to the Lord your God" — and this is what is meant in the Mishnah (Avot 3:14), "Beloved are Israel, for they are called sons to the Omnipresent." It is known that a person's love for his son stems from the fact that he begot him, especially if he is a firstborn son or a son of his old age. And the Holy One, blessed be He, out of His mercy upon us, chose us out of the seventy nations and called us a firstborn son, as we shall elaborate further on regarding the Holy One, blessed be He's love for Israel. Without doubt, the creation of the first man originally was an act of will and free favor; and since His way is to do good, just as the creation of the entire world was an act of will and free favor so that His greatness might be recognized, as the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Bo 42b) — that the essential purpose of Atzilut was "so that they might know Him" — and since the Holy One, blessed be He, created him in His image as we explained, in the manner that a father gives his own likeness to his son, so to speak, in this manner is the creation of the soul; and the creation of the body is a mold and pattern and garment for the soul, which is the cause and source for the body, and the body is not the cause of the soul. And certainly His love, blessed be He, for man, in bestowing upon him life and abundance and blessing and all good, is in the manner that a father loves his son — for every cause desires to bestow upon its effect, in the manner our sages, of blessed memory, said (Pesachim 112a), "more than the calf wishes to nurse, the cow wishes to nurse it." At times the cow, or the mother, may be prevented from nursing her child if she is ill and unable to nurse; so too at times the supernal flow may be withheld from man — not from His side, blessed be He, for He always bestows like a father who loves his son — but rather from the side of the son, who lacks the readiness to receive; and when man rectifies himself with regard to the soul, he becomes rectified and becomes a fit vessel to receive the supernal light. Thus the reality of this love is found from the topmost of the levels to their very end.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:16: This matter the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in parashat Va'etchanan (267b), in the passage we quoted at the beginning of chapter 2, where he said: Come and see, all is called love, and it is for the sake of love that all exists. He said "all is called love," meaning that the whole of Atzilut is called love; and he said "it is for the sake of love that all exists," meaning that were it not for the love that every cause has for its effect, to bestow upon it, the world would cease to exist. Thus the world would return to formlessness and void, for all the grades are bound one to another and to another from the topmost of the grades to their very end; and if it should occur to one's mind that Keter might withhold from bestowing upon Chochmah, this would bring about the destruction of the world — for Chochmah would then have nothing with which to bestow upon Binah, nor Binah upon the [lower] extremities, nor Malchut upon Beriah. For this reason it says: the yod's tip [the crown-tip of the letter yod] is never separated from the yod, forever, for it dwells upon it in love. He was precise in his language, not saying "the yod's tip is never separated from the tip that is above it forever" — for that would express the desire of the effect to nurse from its cause, which is certainly a plain matter — that every effect needs its cause to sustain it so that it may live, and therefore it is never separated from it, and its love is with it. Rather, the novelty here is that Keter, which is the tip of the yod — that tip which is Keter — does not need the yod; nevertheless it is not separated from the yod, which is Chochmah, in order to bestow upon it. In this manner, yod and heh are never separated, for they are joined to each other in love; and likewise vav and heh — this one [vav] is always a bridegroom to the bride [heh], for their way is in love. It does not say "heh in vav," to indicate the male's desire to bestow, etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:17: He then returned to explain the bond of the whole of Atzilut: yod in heh, heh in vav, vav in heh — for since he had only explained the bond of yod in heh and vav in heh, he therefore said that vav is bound to the final heh only because the first heh, which is the Mother, bestows upon the Son, who is the vav, and is bound with him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:18: He said at the end of the passage: "therefore all is called love, and this is bound to that in love." These words seem entirely redundant at first glance, since they had already been stated. But it may be said, as we have explained, that the reality of this love is the bond between cause and effect, in order to bestow, in the manner of a father to a son; if so, even from Malchut down to Beriah, and all the grades of Beriah, this aspect applies down to the end of all the grades. Therefore he returned and said, "all is called love, this is bound to that" — meaning, all the effects are bound one to another in a twofold bond: the cause's love in bestowing upon the effect, and the effect's love in nursing from its cause.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:19: He said: "and therefore, whoever loves the King is thereby bound in that love; and therefore, 'And you shall love the Lord your God.'" The explanation is that the name YHVH is called on account of His being the being of all beings in the world; yet nevertheless He is not called the God of the angels or the God of the celestial spheres, but rather "the God of Israel" — that is, "your God," who prides Himself in you and wishes to be called your God. If so, just as He loves you, so is it fitting that you should love Him. And how is it possible that He should be related so as to be called "your God" — that His Godliness, blessed be He, is bound up with man? This is surely through the soul, which is a part of Him, placed within man; through this He has a bond by which His Shechinah and His Godliness are bound with us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:20: With this, the verse (Deuteronomy 4:4), "But you who cleave to the Lord your God are all alive today," may be understood. The intent is that the verse comes to explain how we cleave to Him, blessed be He, saying that we are still alive, and our life-force is through the soul which is His within us, is from Him; through this we cleave to Him and He cleaves to us. And the proof that He cleaves to us is that the soul is in His hand to take at any moment, as it is written (Job 12:10), "in whose hand is the soul of every living thing," and as it is written (Daniel 5:23), "and the God in whose hand is your breath..." And just as our eyes see many times how healthy people die suddenly — this surely shows His cleaving, blessed be He, to us through the soul, for He removes it whenever He wishes.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:21: Regarding the aspect of the soul placed within us, which is a part of Him, blessed be He, the Holy One, blessed be He, is called a companion [rei'a] to us, as the verse says (Proverbs 27:10), "Your friend and your father's friend..." — and He is called "friend" because there are three partners in the making of a person: his father, his mother, and the Holy One, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:22: The Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Beshalach 55b) that this is said of (Proverbs 17:17), "A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity" — in these words: Rabbi Chizkiyah opened and said, regarding this verse, "a friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity" — "a friend loves at all times" is the Holy One, blessed be He, of whom it is written, "do not forsake your friend and your father's friend." "And a brother is born for adversity" — at the time your enemies distress you, what does the Holy One, blessed be He, say? (Psalms 122:8) "For the sake of my brothers and friends, let me now speak peace within you" — not "peace to you" but "within you," for Israel is called brothers and friends to the Holy One, blessed be He. What does "born" mean here — is he then born now? Rather, at a time of distress, a brother is born in the world — a brother arises to correspond to you, to save you from all who distress you. Rabbi Yehudah said: "is born" means that the Holy Supernal King is aroused with this strength to take vengeance for you against the nation on that [other] side, as it says (Exodus 15:2), "My strength and song is Yah, and He has become my salvation" — to arouse [His] mighty deeds against the nations of the world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:23: Rabbi Yesa opened and said: how much is a person obligated to love the Holy One, blessed be He! For the Holy One, blessed be He, has no service except love, and whoever loves Him and serves Him with love, the Holy One, blessed be He, calls him "friend." If so, how do we then explain this verse, "do not forsake your friend and your father's friend," and it is written (Proverbs 25:17), "Let your foot rarely be in your friend's house"? Rather, the colleagues have already established this verse (Chagigah 7a) as referring to burnt offerings. Now, "do not forsake your friend and your father's friend" — to serve Him and to cling to Him and to perform His commandments — "do not forsake," indeed. And as for what is said, "let your foot rarely be in your friend's house," it means, restrain your inclination so that it does not seethe against you and does not rule over you, and do not engage in improper thoughts. "In your friend's house" — what is "your friend's house"? This is the holy soul that your Friend brought into you and placed within you. Therefore the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, is to love Him in all ways, as it is written, "And you shall love the Lord your God." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:24: This passage makes clear how great is the Holy One, blessed be He's, love for man, and especially for Israel, that He, blessed be He, is called brother and friend to each and every one, and collectively, "for the sake of my brothers and friends"; therefore it is fitting that you should love Him — this is "a friend loves at all times," and likewise "your friend and your father's friend, do not forsake."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:25: He explained the matter of forsaking through one of three things: "to serve Him," "to cling to Him," and "to perform His commandments" — it may be said that these correspond to nefesh, ru'ach, neshamah, whose secret is action, speech, and thought, as we elaborated in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 3. And although in the passage they are not in this order — "to serve Him" and "to perform His commandments" appear, seeming at first to be a redundant repetition of the same idea in different words — rather it seems that "to serve Him" refers to the service of prayer, which depends on speech, as the verse calls prayer "service," saying (Deuteronomy 11:13), "and to serve Him with all your heart" — and our sages, of blessed memory, asked, is there service in the heart? Rather, this is prayer. "To cling to Him" is the clinging of thought, for clinging is only through thought and the heart's contemplation, as it says (Genesis 34:3), "and his soul clung," and similarly, as explained above in the previous chapters. "To perform His commandments" are the commandments that depend on action, such as tzitzit, tefillin, charity, and the like.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:26: Corresponding to these three he mentioned in the warning, "let your foot rarely be in your friend's house" — "restrain your inclination so that it does not seethe against you" refers to action, for the seething of the body through the kindling of the inclination is certainly action, and included in this is if one heats himself up in anger, for the soul and the Holy One, blessed be He, flee from him. "And does not rule over you" refers to damaging speech, such as slander and idle talk and the like. "And do not engage in improper thoughts" is thought itself. Each of these three causes the Shechinah to depart from him, so that it finds no place to rest, for the fine spiritual [presence] rests only in a soul that is clean and pure of all dross. And see what the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in parashat Terumah (128a), which we quoted in chapter 4, that after several preparations he mentioned for acquiring the holy spirit, he said: a person should walk in a straight path, not turning to the right or the left; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:27: Regarding these three aspects, he was precise in his wording at the end of the passage: "and therefore, the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, is to love Him in all things" — meaning, in all three aspects mentioned — "as it is written, 'And you shall love the Lord your God.'" And the intent certainly refers to the conclusion of the verse, "with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might," which are themselves the three mentioned. "With all your heart" is thought, for the heart is the root of contemplations and thoughts. "With all your soul" is speech, as it is written (Genesis 2:7), "and man became a living soul," which the Targum renders, "and it became in man a speaking spirit." "With all your might" is action — that with his money he should perform charity and acts of lovingkindness, and the many actions that depend on money; for through money many commandments that depend on action are fulfilled, such as tzitzit, tefillin, sukkah, lulav, and the like, for it is common for a person to perform and fulfill these commandments by means of his money.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:28: When a person contemplates with his intellect what is stated in these verses mentioned, he will see that they are matters close to reason. For it is well known that two brothers are naturally inclined to love one another, because at a time of distress a brother will exert all his effort to save his brother and will risk his life for him. And indeed the Holy One, blessed be He, in this respect is a brother to us, to save us from several distresses, as mentioned in the passage: "a brother arises to correspond to you, to save you." Likewise, the love of friends for one another stems from their mutual assistance in worldly matters and in matters of Torah, as it says (Ecclesiastes 4:9), "Two are better than one"; and when two friends, when one feels that his friend loves him from the heart to the very soul, he will love him in return, and to him he will reveal the secrets of his heart, and whatever he can do to benefit him he will do — especially if this friend had already previously done good for his father and his father's father, so that his love is known to be from the heart and not superficial, then it is incumbent upon this second friend to do good for that friend and to fulfill his will.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:29: All these aspects exist in the Holy One, blessed be He, who partners with man from his mother's womb until his day of death, saving him from many illnesses, from many forms of death, from many distresses, and doing good for him by preparing his sustenance and the like, as Rabbeinu Bachya elaborated in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Contemplation, ch. 5) on the aspects of the Holy One, blessed be He's, goodness to man. And just as He does good for him, so He did good for his father and his father's father — this is "your friend and your father's friend" — He is a faithful friend whose love is known, and it is fitting that you not forsake Him, and likewise it is fitting that you not provoke Him nor be ungrateful for His favors. Therefore He commanded, saying, "let your foot rarely be in your friend's house" — for your friend, who is the Holy One, blessed be He, has a house that He comes to dwell in with you, namely his soul placed within man's body; and if the soul is damaged in one of the three things mentioned — through evil thoughts, or through speech of slander and the like, or by transgressing one of the negative commandments — then the house is filled with idols, and the King, who is spiritual and holy, flees from there, as explained in the Tikkunim (3b), that He does not rest upon a damaged soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:30: He was precise in saying "do not engage in improper thoughts," meaning that one should not bring himself to improper thought at all — as it is written in the Gemara (Niddah 13b), whoever brings himself to improper thought is not admitted into the domain of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Psalms 5:5), "evil shall not sojourn with You" — and it follows of itself, certainly, that the Holy One, blessed be He, will not rest in the dwelling-house of His soul in this world, in this body, since it is damaged.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:31: The two verses mentioned — "your friend and your father's friend, do not forsake," and the verse "let your foot rarely be" — although at first glance their meaning is one, namely to warn one not to do things that would cause the friend to flee from him, nevertheless the verse "your friend and your father's friend, do not forsake" concerns the positive aspect, as it is written, "do not forsake, to serve Him," etc. From the physical friend we may understand the spiritual: for it is known that between two friends, one greater than the other, who has done good for him — if he comes to dwell in his house, reason dictates that he must prepare a fine lodging for him and clear the dwelling of everything repulsive, as it is said (Genesis 24:31), "Come, blessed of the Lord; why do you stand outside, when I have cleared the house?" And if these conditions are lacking, that friend will distance himself from him. Therefore David the king, peace be upon him, said elsewhere (Psalms 34:15), "Turn from evil and do good." Therefore, regarding the positive aspect, Solomon the king, peace be upon him, said, "do not forsake" [i.e., do not cease] from doing good, namely "to serve Him," etc. And by inference from the negative you understand the positive — the intent being to say, do not forsake Him so that He leaves as He came, but rather hold fast to Him so that He clings to you. And by what means do you hold fast to Him? By engaging in Torah and commandments and purity of thought — and He is, so to speak, compelled to come dwell with you, for you hold fast to Him firmly, making Him a fine bed and a fine, perfumed dwelling with many kinds of spices, and the friend finds contentment there, and surely there he will cling.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:32: This is what David the king, peace be upon him, intended in saying (Psalms 101:2), "I will contemplate the way of the blameless — when will You come to me? I will walk within my house with a whole heart" — the meaning being that he was awaiting the holy spirit that used to rest upon him at midnight, when a north wind would blow upon David's harp and it would play, and then he would awaken and the holy spirit would rest upon him, as our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Berachot 3b). And in order that the holy spirit find a place to rest, he would make prior preparation, namely "I will walk within my house with a whole heart," and by saying "within my house" he indicates the soul dwelling within his body, which is his house — in the manner we explained in the passage, that "your friend's house" is the soul. We already quoted in the Gate of Fear, chapter 11, the passage from Ra'aya Meheimna (Shoftim 275a) explaining that the stones of his house are his 248 limbs.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:33: It follows that the essential dwelling of the Shechinah is only in the pure soul, and this is (Exodus 25:8), "And let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them" — it does not say "within it" but "among them," meaning within their inward being. This is one aspect of the matter of man's creation, through the soul, which is a part of God from above, and through it the Holy One, blessed be He, clings to man to save him, and when he calls upon Him, He answers him, as it is written (Proverbs 17:17), "and a brother is born for adversity," and similarly (Psalms 91:15), "He shall call upon Me and I shall answer him; I am with him in distress and I will deliver him." And this is an aspect [present] in Israel more than in the nations.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:34: When a person contemplates this matter, his soul will be enkindled with love, and he will say in his heart: is it fitting that I, a person formed of matter, dust and ashes, should have the Holy One, blessed be He — whom the heavens of heavens cannot contain — wish to dwell with me? Who am I, that the Supernal King should come to dwell in my house? It is fitting that I make a fine dwelling for Him, so that He may come to dwell with me — in the manner David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 101:2), "When will You come to me," etc., referring, as explained, to engaging in Torah. And when one who engages in Torah knows what the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Bereishit 50a), that Torah scholars who separate from their wives during the six weekdays to engage in Torah — the Supernal Union unites with them, and does not separate from them, etc. — and this is the Shechinah — it is fitting that their hearts be enkindled to love her as a man loves his beloved, and to make her a fine dwelling in his heart, etc., in the manner explained in the Tikkunim which we quoted in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 7, so that the Shechinah may find a place to rest, for she does not dwell in a damaged place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:35: It may be said that the Shechinah is called "your friend," in the manner we explained in chapter 4, that our sages, of blessed memory, explained that regarding the female too it is said (Leviticus 19:18), "and you shall love your friend as yourself" — and she is called "your friend" because she partners with those below forever, giving them their sustenance and their food and all their needs; and she is "your father's friend," namely the Holy One, blessed be He, for the governance of the world is through both of them together, as it is said (Psalms 89:15), "Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:36: With this, what the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained on the verse (Proverbs 17:17), "a friend loves at all times," and "a brother" — is the Holy One, blessed be He — may be reconciled, though both are titles for one attribute, requiring distinction between them. Indeed, according to this approach, that "friend" is the Shechinah, and she is called "the friend" with the definite article, it is well reconciled: "brother" corresponds to Tiferet, who is called "brother," and she is "sister." It would also be possible to explain this regarding Binah, for the secret of "friends" [in the plural] is Chochmah and Binah (Zohar, parashat Vayikra 4a); and she is called "your friend" with regard to her expansion into the six extremities, and "your father's friend" with regard to her union with Abba [Chochmah], from whom she is never separated. Nevertheless, the surface meaning of the passage is better reconciled with the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, as the discerning reader will see.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:37: The second aspect concerning man's sustenance: our sages, of blessed memory, said (Ta'anit 2a), in these words: Rabbi Yochanan said, three keys are in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, that were not given over to any agent, and these are: the key of rains, the key of childbirth, and the key of the resurrection of the dead. The key of rains, as it is written (Deuteronomy 28:12), "The Lord will open for you His good treasury, the heavens, to give the rain of your land in its season." The key of childbirth, from where do we know it? As it is said (Genesis 30:22), "And God remembered Rachel... and He opened her womb." The key of the resurrection of the dead, from where do we know it? (Ezekiel 37:13), "And you shall know that I am the Lord, when I open your graves." In the West [Eretz Yisrael] they say: also the key of sustenance, as it is written (Psalms 145:16), "You open Your hand," etc. And why did Rabbi Yochanan not count this one? He would say to you: rains are themselves sustenance. — end of quotation.
